heroHeadline: SAC Massacres 133+ in Kanbalu Double Airstrike — KIA Seizes Bhamo Tank Battalion as Battle Stalemates; AA Vows Sittwe and Kyaukphyu by 2027 — Day 1,950
heroSubtitle: On Day 1,950 (June 5, 2026), Myanmar's civil war has intensified across all five active fronts: SAC fighter jets conducted a catastrophic double airstrike on Kanbalu Township, Sagaing Region on June 3, killing 133+ civilians — the aircraft returned at 5:30 PM to strike rescuers at the same location, in one of the deadliest single-day attacks since the 2021 coup. The Battle of Bhamo has entered a stalemate phase: KIA seized a junta tank battalion near the airport and destroyed a radar system at Myitkyina Air Base on June 4, but the KIA itself acknowledges that the SAC's unprecedented 50 daily airstrikes have prevented KIA from completing the city's final encirclement — the highest concentration of junta air power in Kachin State since the coup. In Rakhine, Arakan Army Commander Twan Mrat Naing vowed to capture all remaining junta-held towns (Sittwe, Kyaukphyu, and Manaung) before 2027, following AA forces killing 40+ junta soldiers around Sittwe's western naval bases (May 29–June 1); the AA now controls 14 of Rakhine's 17 townships and maintains positions within 5km of China's $7.3B Kyaukphyu CMEC port. Myanmar President Min Aung Hlaing returned from India on June 3, completing his five-day state visit — the SAC's most successful diplomatic normalization since the coup — while his forces simultaneously massacred civilians across Sagaing and pressed multi-front offensives in Kachin, Rakhine, and Chin. The International Crisis Group published a major briefing (N°188) characterizing the new SAC civilian government as 'military consolidation, not transition.' IDPs have reached approximately 5.2 million — the highest since the 2021 coup.
